Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking the time last week. As discussed, we're putting together the procurement packet for ShopLytics' ranking pipeline and need a clear baseline for hosted API pricing for your rerank / classifier endpoints. A few specifics we need in writing:

- Baseline per-item scoring price for the hosted reranker (we score ~3–20 candidates per query). Please state whether you bill per-scored candidate or per-invocation and how you handle multi-candidate payloads.
- Classifier pricing for single-label classification (per-document) and multi-label (if different).
- Volume tiers / committed discounts (1M, 5M, 10M scored items per month).
- Any separate charges for prefix caching, KV cache retention, or additional per-token charges we should model.
- Estimated monthly total for a pilot: 500k queries/month, avg 6 candidates/query, 2 tokens/label on average for classifier calls.
- Security/compliance notes (SOC2 + data residency).

Can you share a short PDF rate card and an example calculation for the pilot estimate? We also want to know typical lead times for moving from hosted to a Dedicated pool (if we outgrow hosted economics).

Attaching our RFP summary and current traffic snapshot.

Appreciate it — Andrea

Hi Andrea — great to hear from you and thanks for the RFP. Short answer first, then a worked example for the pilot. Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk the numbers.

Summary pricing (hosted Redwood API):
- Rerank (per-scored candidate): $0.00095 per scored candidate for our baseline curated models. For higher-accuracy model variants we list at $0.0018 per candidate.
- Classifier (per document): $0.00085 per document for single-label. Multi-label classifiers billed at $0.0014 per document (reflects additional compute/IO).
- Billing unit: we invoice on scored items (each candidate evaluated by the rerank model counts as one scored item). A single API call with N candidates = N scored items.

Volume discounts (hosted API / annual payment profile):
- 0–1M scored items/mo: list price
- 1M–5M: 15% off list
- 5M–20M: 25% off list
- 20M+: please contact us for Dedicated/reserved pricing (significant step function)

Pilot estimate example (500k queries/mo, avg 6 candidates/query):
- Scored items = 500k * 6 = 3,000,000 scored items
- At 3M items -> falls in 1M–5M tier, 15% discount on rerank price
- Rerank cost (baseline model): 3,000,000 * $0.00095 * 0.85 = $2,423.
- Classifier (assume 500k docs): 500,000 * $0.00085 = $425.
- Estimated monthly total (hosted) ~= $2,848 (ex-tax).

Notes and clarifications:
- There are no separate "per-token" surcharges for rerank scoring; however, sequence length materially affects model selection. If your candidate text lengths are large, we may recommend a different model variant with different unit pricing.
- KV/prefix caching is included in hosted plans; additional long-term cache retention or dedicated cache pods are part of Dedicated offers.
- SOC2 and EU data residency: Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified and can restrict hosted inference to specific regions. We can provide the compliance pack and evidence for procurement — copying Neha on this thread.
- Transition to Dedicated: typical lead time is 6–10 weeks for capacity and onboarding, shorter with an active commitment and upfront payment.

I'll attach a short rate card PDF with the tiers and sample calculations. If you want a more aggressive commercial (deeper discount for a 12-month commit), let us know target ARR/volume and we can model.

Would Thursday or Friday this week for a 30-min call work?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales — Platform
Redwood Inference

Folks — looping you in to discuss the ShopLytics ask (DL-4389). Key points from Andrea:

- Pilot ~500k queries/mo with avg 6 candidates -> ~3M scored items/month.
- They want pricing for both rerank and classifiers and clarity on billing units (they explicitly asked whether we bill per call or per-candidate).
- SOC2 + residency is a gating item for procurement.

My draft commercial thinking:
- Offer the baseline hosted pricing I sent above but include an introductory commercial: 18% off for a 12-month commit at their pilot volume (DL-4389) instead of 15%. We can do 18% if we include a 3-month ramp credit (one-time credit = $2,000) and require a modest MRR commit (recommendation: minimum $1,500/mo).
- If they commit to 12 months and >10M scored items total across the year we should push them toward Dedicated; margin will be better for us and gives them predictable latency/SLOs.

Margin / risk notes:
- At 18% discount and pilot volumes, blended gross margin still healthy (~55–60%) given small inference footprint but avoid deeper discounts without committed spend.
- If they ask for reserved QPS or node guarantees, escalate to Solutions Eng for sizing; pricing will shift materially.

Next steps: I can send the formal commercial PDF + 12-month term sheet. Neha — can you prepare the compliance pack (SOC2 + region controls)? Marcus — can you run a quick sensitivity showing our margin at 15%, 18%, 25% discounts for the projected 3M/month baseline?

Thanks,
Kim
